title: Meet
Marlo
paragraphs: Marlo grew up above a harbour-side chip shop, peeling potatoes before school and learning to judge a batter by the sound it makes in the fryer. The pufferfish on our sign was the first thing Marlo ever doodled on an order pad, and it stuck.

After years cooking in other people's kitchens, Marlo opened Tide & Chips with one rule: fry it fresh, serve it hot, and never rush the chips. Come by, say hello and ask for the batter recipe. You won't get it, but you will get an extra lemon wedge.

testimonials.lede: A few notes from the folks who sat down, ate up and left us the crumbs.

items.quote: I came for the chips and stayed for the batter. Crispy outside, soft inside, and the lemon wedge was exactly the right size. Rare.
items.name: Jo

items.quote: Best fish and chips by the water. We ate on the wall and the seagulls respected us.
items.name: Priya

items.quote: The pufferfish on the sign made my kid laugh. The chips made my kid quiet. Perfect.
items.name: Sam

items.quote: Fast, hot and not greasy. Ordered extra tartare and have no regrets.
